name: ADS1115 16-bit 4-channel ADC
description: Texas Instruments 16-bit delta-sigma analog-to-digital converter with 4 single-ended (or 2 differential) inputs, a programmable gain amplifier (full-scale ±0.256 V to ±6.144 V) and 8–860 samples/s, read over I2C. Runs on 2.0–5.5 V; inputs must stay between GND and VDD. Sold as: ADS1115 16-bit 4-channel ADC module, blue 10-pin breakout (GY-ADS1115 / HW-526 clone of the original Adafruit #1085), 10-pin header VDD, GND, SCL, SDA, ADDR, ALRT, A0, A1, A2, A3; I2C address 0x48 (ADDR to GND), 0x49 (VDD), 0x4A (SDA), 0x4B (SCL).
eli5: Measures voltages very precisely (to about a tenth of a millivolt) on four inputs and tells your board the numbers over two wires.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 2.0–5.5 V. Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico: the board's SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VDD

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (also the reference for single-ended readings)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10k pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10k pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: ADDR
pins.description: Address select: GND (pulled down on the board) = 0x48, VDD = 0x49, SDA = 0x4A, SCL = 0x4B

pins.name: ALRT
pins.description: ALERT/RDY open-drain output (comparator / conversion ready), not needed for basic use

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Analog input AIN0, GND to VDD (never more than VDD + 0.3 V)

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Analog input AIN1, GND to VDD

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Analog input AIN2, GND to VDD

pins.name: A3
pins.description: Analog input AIN3, GND to VDD

buildNotes: Single-shot read: write Config (pointer 0x01) with OS=1, the input MUX, PGA, MODE=1 and DR, wait 1/data-rate (7.8 ms at 128 SPS), poll until Config bit 15 (OS) reads 1, then read the Conversion register (pointer 0x00).
The result is a signed 16-bit code: volts = code × FSR / 32768, e.g. 125 µV per count at ±4.096 V. Single-ended inputs only use the positive half (0 to 32767).
Never put more than VDD + 0.3 V (or less than −0.3 V) on A0–A3, whatever gain you choose. Divide larger voltages down with resistors first.
Power the module from 3.3 V when using an ESP32 or Pico: its I2C pull-ups go to VDD, and 5 V on SDA/SCL can damage 3.3 V GPIOs.
Leave ADDR unconnected (pulled to GND on the board) for 0x48; tie it to VDD, SDA or SCL for 0x49/0x4A/0x4B to use up to four modules on one bus.
Join the GND of the signal you measure to the module's GND.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ads1115 import ADS1115

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
adc = ADS1115(i2c, fsr=4.096)  # address 0x48, +/-4.096 V range (125 uV per count)
while True:
    raw = adc.read_raw(0)
    print('A0 raw=%d V=%.3f' % (raw, adc.raw_to_volts(raw)))
    time.sleep(1)
